scope: Two independent native-source backgrounds converted through the shipped structural methods into separate editable schema-12 projects and generated NROM static viewers. Files preserve source identity and recovery evidence. Generated viewers use canonical palette normalization and rendering defaults; they do not reconstruct original game engines, collision, entities, animation, audio or native program behavior. Generation verifies detached preview and ordinary saved-project ROM equality; runtime pixel verification is in tests/re-native-background.cjs. Browser and physical hardware acceptance are not established.

outputs.name: Pepsi

source.description: Independent Pepsi vending native ROM; bounded reset-linked immediate PPU construction.

limitations: One static background and its physical CHR bank only. Sprites, scrolling, animation, collision, actors, audio and game logic are not recovered.
Import adds an editable scene excluded from the current build. Download background project creates a separate Forge static viewer; it does not recreate the original program.
The source ROM is unchanged. There is no native ROM patch, inverse encoder or whole-game reconstruction claim.
Forge displays the underlying 256 × 240 background with its own rendering mask. Original clipping, sprite overlays and later runtime writes are not reproduced.

One reset-linked, forced-blank initialization with immediate PPU palette writes and a literal/counted-fill nametable subroutine is supported. Arbitrary 6502 code, indirect pointers and other compression are not interpreted.
This is the initialized background only. Later text, sprites, input, game logic, raster effects, collisions and audio are not recovered.
Canonical conversion builds a separate Forge static scene. There is no native encoder, source-ROM patch, inverse or byte-round-trip claim.
Only a proven static NROM background pattern bank, nametable zero, zero scroll and unemphasized nongrayscale background rendering are supported.

outputs.name: HonkeyPong

source.description: Independent HonkeyPong native ROM reproduced from the external source checkpoint; bounded pointer/page nametable construction.

limitations: One static background and its physical CHR bank only. Sprites, scrolling, animation, collision, actors, audio and game logic are not recovered.
Import adds an editable scene excluded from the current build. Download background project creates a separate Forge static viewer; it does not recreate the original program.
The source ROM is unchanged. There is no native ROM patch, inverse encoder or whole-game reconstruction claim.
Forge displays the underlying 256 × 240 background with its own rendering mask. Original clipping, sprite overlays and later runtime writes are not reproduced.
Recognizes the declared vector-linked four-state dispatch and pointer-page nametable/palette loader routines, not arbitrary NES engines or compressed maps.
Recovers the matched upload phase: 1023 nametable/attribute writes. The last attribute byte retains unknown prior PPU state and is marked unknown; zero is an explicit conversion placeholder.
The native loader uses Y=$FF as its page stop without resetting Y. Source bytes at page boundaries are reordered; the exact source-index write sequence is preserved.
Native PPUMASK=$18 clips the leftmost eight background pixels; an editable map can show the underlying tiles. No complete runtime frame or original gameplay behavior is promised.
Sprites, collision, animation, dynamic score/text writes and subsequent runtime changes are not recovered. Original ROM bytes remain unchanged.

The native loader leaves 1 attribute byte(s) dependent on prior PPU state (nametable indices 1023). The Forge conversion explicitly fills them with zero; these values are authored defaults, not recovered source data.
